chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a man does not find a purifier (water) and he is in a state of major impurity (junub), let him wipe from the earth (perform tayammum) and pray. So when he finds water, let him perform ghusl, and the prayer he has already prayed will suffice him.'

key_terms.أَجْزَأَتْهُ: It sufficed him / was accepted for him
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: One in a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.طَهُورٌ: Purifier (specifically referring to water for ritual purification)
key_terms.يَمْسَحْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ: To wipe from the earth (the action of tayammum)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person in a state of junub who performs tayammum and then finds water?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'validity of the act performed' (istishab al-hukm) in Shia jurisprudence, confirming that the initial tayammum suffices for the prayer even if water becomes available later, without requiring repetition. It highlights the practical ease (taysir) granted to the junub when water is inaccessible, emphasizing that the subsequent ghusl is for the state of purity rather than a condition for the validity of the already-completed prayer. This ruling is foundational in distinguishing between the obligation of ghusl and the permissibility of praying via tayammum in cases of necessity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘When the man does not find cleanliness and he was with sexual impurity, so let him wipe from the earth, and he should pray Salaat. So when he does find water, so let him wash, and his Salaat would suffice him, which he prayed’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘

If means of cleansing (water for Ghusl (bath)) cannot be found after experiencing sexual relation, one must wipe one’s face with (soil for Tayammum) earth, then perform Salah (prayer). When water is found, Ghusl (bath) must be taken and Salah (prayer) so performed is sufficient.’”
